state.misconception_label: Does not know the properties of a rectangle

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: The angles highlighted on this rectangle with different length sides can never be... ![A rectangle with the diagonals drawn in. The angle on the right hand side at the centre is highlighted in red and the angle at the bottom at the centre is highlighted in yellow.](). I got acute because I assumed all the angles in the figure are equal.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The properties of a rectangle include having four right angles. In a rectangle, opposite angles are equal, so if one angle is acute, the opposite angle will also be acute. Make sure to consider all the properties of a rectangle when determining the angles in the figure.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the four corners of the rectangle are all 90 degrees - I get that now. But I'm still confused about those angles in the middle where the diagonals cross... are those the ones we're looking at? Because those don't look like 90 degrees to me.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Yes, you are correct that the four corners of a rectangle have angles of 90 degrees. When the diagonals of a rectangle intersect, they create four right angles at the point of intersection. This property is unique to rectangles and can help you identify them in different figures.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, but the diagonals crossing at right angles... is that always true for rectangles? Because I thought I learned that about squares, not rectangles? And looking at the diagram again, those angles in the middle don't actually look like 90 degrees to me - one looks wider and one looks narrower.

score.justification_pass1: The teacher makes a critical mathematical error by claiming diagonals of rectangles intersect at right angles (only true for squares), fails to engage with the student's correct observation that the angles don't look like 90 degrees, and provides answers rather than prompting reasoning, leaving the student more confused than at the start.
score.justification_pass2: While the teacher states some rules about rectangle properties, they provide incorrect information (claiming diagonals of rectangles intersect at right angles, which is only true for squares) and fail to give explicit procedural steps or direct corrective feedback on the student's specific misconception about the angles at the diagonal intersection.
